What we treat

Everything that hurts, under one roof

Two doctors of chiropractic, with massage and rehab therapy in the same building — so the adjustment, the soft-tissue work and the exercises that keep it from coming back all happen in one place. Tap any of the four to see what's inside it.

The adjustment itself. Dr. Anderson and Dr. Durrance both see general patients, and patients keep going back to whichever doctor they've come to know.

  • Neck pain
  • Back and shoulder pain
  • Headaches
  • Herniated discs
  • Extremity pain — hips, knees, shoulders

Rear-ended on 410 and stiff the next morning. Call the front desk before you decide it'll work itself out.

  • Auto accident injuries
  • Whiplash and neck strain
  • Personal injury care
  • Gentle adjusting, plus stretches and rehab built around the injury

Lifted wrong on the job, or the same motion eight hours a day for years. Bring the claim paperwork and the desk will walk you through it.

  • On-the-job injuries
  • Repetitive-use injuries
  • Worker's-comp claims
  • Strengthening work so it holds up when you go back

The part that decides whether you're back in three weeks — soft tissue, strengthening, and what you do between visits.

  • Massage therapy for musculoskeletal pain
  • Better circulation, less swelling, more range of motion
  • Corrective exercises you keep doing at home
  • Rehab therapy in the same building as the adjustment

Covered? Auto-accident, worker's-comp and most major insurance plans are handled here every day. Call the front desk with your card and they'll check your plan for you before you come in.

Inside the office

There's a whole room behind the adjusting table

Mirrors, exercise balls, a seated rehab machine and a drawer of resistance bands — the strengthening half of the work happens in the building, in front of a doctor, before it ever becomes homework.

The doctors

A plateau kid who never left

Dan Anderson graduated from Enumclaw High School in 1982, came back with a Doctorate of Chiropractic from Western States in 1988, and has been adjusting his neighbors ever since.

Three decades on the same stretch of Hwy 410 means a lot of his patients have been coming since before their kids could drive. His own bio puts the whole practice in one sentence: the positive energy and charisma his patients look to him for, right alongside the treatment.

Dr. Jordan Durrance joined him as the practice's second doctor. He played baseball at Pepperdine, and found chiropractic the hard way — a severe low-back injury on a high-school baseball trip to Australia. He graduated Cum Laude from Life Chiropractic College West. Outside the office he's outnumbered at home by his wife Nicole and their three kids, Jamison, Colton and Vaylin.

Where it hurts

Point at it, and we’ll tell you what that visit looks like

Tap the part of you that has been talking. Tap it again to clear it.

Tap where it hurts

Nothing here is a diagnosis. It is simply what this practice treats in that spot, and what it has in the building for it.

Head & neck

Neck pain, headaches, and the whiplash that shows up the morning after a collision — all three sit on the practice’s own list of what it treats.

The soft-tissue side of it is handled by the massage therapy in this same building, not by a referral across town.

Say “neck” when you call · (253) 862-2138 ↗

Shoulders & upper back

Back and shoulder pain, plus the shoulder end of what the practice files under extremity pain.

Their own walkthrough video is a doctor holding one end of a resistance band for this exact area — that is what the strengthening work looks like here.

Say “shoulder” when you call · (253) 862-2138 ↗

Mid back & ribs

Herniated discs are named here, and so are the repetitive-use injuries that come from doing one motion on the job for twenty years.

If it started at work, say so on the phone — worker’s-comp is one of the four kinds of care the practice lists.

Say “mid back” when you call · (253) 862-2138 ↗

Low back

Low-back pain, and the auto-accident and worker’s-comp cases that so often arrive as exactly this and nothing else.

The at-home strengthening half is treated as part of the plan, not as something extra you get talked into.

Say “low back” when you call · (253) 862-2138 ↗

Hips, knees & ankles

The practice does not stop at the spine — hips and knees are on the list under extremity pain, same as the rest.

Whichever doctor you already know is the one you get booked with; patients here tend to stay with the same one for years.

Say “knee” when you call · (253) 862-2138 ↗

Getting in

Three steps, no portal to log into

  1. Call the front desk

    Amy or Linda picks up. If it's after hours, leave a note below instead.

  2. Say what's going on

    New patient, a car accident, a work claim, or a back that's been talking to you — telling them which one gets you to the right doctor faster.

  3. Pull into the storefront row

    The office sits in the row of shops on Hwy 410 E — the tinted window with the gold lettering is the one.
